items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: that's where I worked with Budd Johnson and Keg Johnson

ctx.x: Well, did you work with Papa Bouchet's band at the Villa DeNice?

Yes, but that was later -- after the Gold Coast job folded, then I joined Eddie Mallory's band and that's where I worked with Budd Johnson and Keg Johnson. But my brother and I split up ways then, because when I went with Milt Senior, he stayed on with the Speed Webb band, so by the time I got to Chicago, I was in Toledo, I was on my own, away from Gus. Since we left school together, we had been together until that period in Toledo.

But in Chicago, it was still a spit away from the Milt Senior band to play with…

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: And we had Teddy Wilson on piano, and they sent for Yank Porter on drums.

ctx.x: Right, that's what I'm trying to get at.

And she wrote some very good songs, and I don't know, I think maybe Irene is still living. I understand she lost her sight, or something, and she's living in Cleveland, Ohio now. But then we all were staying at a woman's house by the name of Mrs. Otter, on South Parkway there, and Mrs. Otter used to cook and feed us, and we would sit up and play cards and Teddy would be showing me changes and things on the piano. They guy rehearsed like four, five, six hours a day.
And I used to go get my horn sometime, and he'd -- I can still play some passages that he showed me, 'Liza,' you know, 'cause 'Liza' was a pretty rough tune to jam on in those days.
